ham-potatoes-and-vegetables-excluding-ca.title: Ham, potatoes and vegetables without carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of boiled or baked potatoes, tender ham, and a mix of vegetables (such as sweet pepper, zucchini, tomatoes), deliberately excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy greens. It contains no sauce, allowing the natural flavors of the ingredients to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ham is smoked or boiled pork meat taken from the hind leg of the pig.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed root vegetables and are rich in starch and vitamin C.
The lack of sauce makes the dish lighter on the stomach and highlights each ingredient’s true taste.
The ham‑and‑potato combination is a staple in many traditional European recipes.
Excluding carrots, broccoli, and leafy greens makes the dish suitable for people with allergies to those vegetables.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ham provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Potatoes and certain vegetables like sweet pepper contain vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, helping maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Low in simple sugars
items.content: Omitting carrots and sauce reduces the overall simple sugar content of the meal.

items.title: Gentle on digestion
items.content: The absence of heavy sauces and leafy greens makes the dish easier on the stomach.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ham is often salty; people with hypertension should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic or intolerant to pork.

items.title: Potato glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, which can raise blood sugar quickly.

items.title: Reduced fiber
items.content: Excluding leafy greens lowers the dietary fiber content of the dish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or side. Cube the potatoes and bake until golden, slice the ham into strips, and lightly sauté the vegetables in olive oil. Mix everything together and enjoy without any sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave to retain vegetable texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Squirrel is a light dry snack made from whole grains roasted to a golden crisp. It has a mild nutty flavor and a crunchy texture, perfect for a quick bite any time of day.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The snack is named “Squirrel” because its shape resembles a tiny nut.
Only whole grains are used, with no artificial flavorings added.
The product is gluten‑free and suitable for people with gluten intolerance.
Squirrel can be stored for up to 12 months when kept properly.
It contains a small amount of salt but no added sugar.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Its protein content makes the snack a good source of energy and helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: The absence of added sugar helps control blood glucose levels.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Grain allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the ingredients.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: People monitoring sodium intake should limit the amount of this snack.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although light, it still provides calories, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Squirrel can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to salads, yogurts, muesli, or used as a crunchy topping for soups and stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool, dark place. After opening, keep the bag tightly sealed to maintain crunchiness and prevent fat oxidation.
